texts.preamble: Vide This Common Judgment vs The State Of Bihar & Another on 28 April, 2018 In the Court of Ms. Poonam A. Bamba, District & Sessions Judge : New Delhi: Patiala House Courts, New Delhi. In the matters of : 1. Fsat No. 43/2016 Sh. Bhumesh Kumar S/o Sh. Ram Nath Supplier M/s Ganpati Trading Company 25/87, Gali No. 14 Vishwas Nagar, Shahdara Delhi110 032 R/o 25/87, Gali No. 14 Vishwas Nagar, Shahdara Delhi110 032. And 2. Fsat No. 44/2016 Sh.Sarfuddin (Proprietor) Fbo (Food Business Operator) S/o Sh. Salamat Khan M/s Aameer Breakfast Corner E166/9, Gali No. 17 Shastri Park, Delhi110 053. R/o E322, Gali No. 10 Shastri Park, Delhi - 110 053. And Fsat No 43/16, 44/16 & 45/16 Bhumesh Kumar, Sarfuddin & Karan Jain V. Fso Page 1 of 16 3. Fsat No. 45/2016 Sh. Karan Jain (Proprietor) Manufacturer M/s Nanaji Bakers and Confectioners 40/7, Street No. 1, Samay Pur Industrial Area Delhi - 110 042 . Versus State Through Sh. Rajender Kumar Bhasker Food Safety Officer Department of Food Safety Govt. of Nct of Delhi 8th Floor, Mayur Bhawan Connaught Place, New Delhi 110 001. ..... Respondent Vide This Common Judgment vs The State Of Bihar & Another on 28 April, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55494564/ 1 Appeals Against The Order Dated 03.06.2016 Of Ld. Adm, District (North East). Date of filing of appeals : 16.07.2016 Arguments concluded on : 19.04.2018 Date of judgment : 28.04.2018 J U D G M E N T : Fsat No 43/16, 44/16 & 45/16 Bhumesh Kumar, Sarfuddin & Karan Jain V. Fso Page 2 of 16 1.0 Vide this common judgment, I shall dispose of all the above three appeals against the same order dated 03.0
texts.facts: . Appellant Bhumesh Kumar (FSAT No. 43/2016) is the proprietor of the Supplier firm M/s Ganpati Trading FSAT No 43/16, 44/16 & 45/16 Bhumesh Kumar, Sarfuddin & Karan Jain V. FSO Page 3 of 16 Company, 25/87, Gali No.14, Vishwas Nagar, Shahdara, Delhi 110032 and the appellant Sarfuddin (FSAT No. 44/2016) is the proprietor of FBO firm namely M/s Aameer Breakfast Corner, E 166/9, Gali No.17, Shastri Park, Delhi110053. 2.0 Facts in brief which are not in dispute are, that: (i) on 7th July, 2015, Food Safety Officer ("FSO" in short), purchased 8 sealed packets of "Zeera Cookies", Vide This Common Judgment vs The State Of Bihar & Another on 28 April, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55494564/ 2 from the possession of appellant Sarfuddin, Proprietor of M/s Aameer Breakfast Corner (FBO firm), where the said food article was found stored for sale for human consumption. One counterpart of the sample under sealed cover was sent to Food Analyst on 08.07.2015. The Food Analyst vide his report dated 22.07.2015 opined the sample as misbranded because of violation of Regulation 2.2.2.10 of FSS (P&L) Regulations. He also found the sample to be misleading as it was violative of Regulation 2.3.1.5 FSS (P&L) Regulations. The Food Analyst also reported that Best before was declared in small letters on outer label as "Best before upto 6 months from the date of packing. FSAT No 43/16, 44/16 & 45/16 Bhumesh Kumar, Sarfuddin & Karan Jain V. FSO Page 4 of 16 Further, nutritional value declared on outer and inner labels are different, which is misleading. Outer label declares contains permitted synthetic food colour (127), which was not detected during analysis"; (ii) a copy of the Food Analyst Report was sent to all the appellants i.e. to FBO, Supplier & Manufacturing Company on 03.08.2015 giving them an opportunity to prefer an appeal against the report of the Food Analyst under Section 46(4) of the FSS Act for sending one part of the sample to the Referral Lab, if so desired. But none of the appellants preferred appeal against the Food Analyst's Report; (iii) appellant Sarfuddin, Proprietor of FBO M/s Aameer Breakfast Corner, at the time of taking sample was looking after the business of the said firm on day to day basis. He submitted an application dated 25.08.2015 that he agreed with the report of the Food Analyst and did not want to challenge the same; (iv) the Food Safety Officer, after going through the FSAT No 43/16, 44/16 & 45/16 Bhumesh Kumar, Sarfuddin & Karan Jain V. FSO Page 5 of 16 facts and the documents, recorded violation of Section 26(1) & 26(2) (ii) read with Section 3(1)(a) &3(1)(zf) (a) of the FSS Act and Regulation 2.2.2.10 rendering it misbranded and that of Regulation 2.3.1.5 of FSS(P&L) Regulations for misleading, which is punishable under Sections 52 and 58 of FSS Act; Vide This Common Judgment vs The State Of Bihar & Another on 28 April, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55494564/ 3 (v) a complaint/application before Ld. ADM was filed. Notices of the same were issued to all the appellants and hearing was given. The appellants admitted aforesaid violations and prayed for leniency. All the appellants have challenged the above order of Ld. ADM dated 03.06.2016 pleading that the impugned order was passed without considering the facts and the evidence on record and without appreciating the law as applicable.
texts.arguments: 3.1 The appellant Bhumesh Kumar/supplier (FAST No. 43/2016) has submitted that he is an FBO and had purchased the sample commodity from the manufacturer Karan Jain, Proprietor of M/s Nanaji Bakers and Confectioners; and that it is the admitted case of the complainant/FSO that the sample commodity was in sealed condition as purchased from the manufacturer (M/s Nanaji Bakers & Confectioners). Hence, he could not have been held liable. FSAT No 43/16, 44/16 & 45/16 Bhumesh Kumar, Sarfuddin & Karan Jain V. FSO Page 7 of 16 3.1.1 Appellant Sarfuddin (FAST No. 44/2016) has also taken a similar plea that the Ld. ADM failed to appreciate that the sample commodity was purchased by him from the supplier/appellant Bhumesh Kumar and was sold in sealed condition. Vide This Common Judgment vs The State Of Bihar & Another on 28 April, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55494564/ 4 3.1.2 Both the above appellants have also pleaded that they cannot be held responsible for printing and declaration on the label of the said commodity. 3.1.3 The appellant Karan Jain/manufacturer (FAST No. 45/2016) has contended that there has been substantial compliance of the regulations 2.2.2.10 of FSS (P&L) Regulations as the required information was printed on the label. No prejudice has been caused to the consumer of the product. Thus, the prosecution launched against the appellants was unwarranted. It is submitted that the information (best before) had been printed in small letters therefore, the appellant cannot be held guilty of misbranding u/S 2(ix)(k) of the PFA Act and placed reliance upon the judgment of Hon'ble Patna High Court in M.D. Anand Aqua, M/s S.B. Industries, FSAT No 43/16, 44/16 & 45/16 Bhumesh Kumar, Sarfuddin & Karan Jain V. FSO Page 8 of 16 Patna Vs. The State of Bihar & another, 2011(1) FAC 265, and that of Hon'ble Jharkhand High Court in Md. Shree Om Industries Vs. State of Jharkhand and another, 2012 (2) FAC 8, Oscar Joseph & another Vs. The State of Jharkhand and another ,2012 FAC 74 and Sri Jalaj Kumar Chatterjee Vs. State of Jharkhand and others, 2013 (1) FAC 482. It is also pleaded that Regulation 2.3.1.5 does not apply to biscuits. It is further submitted that even otherwise, the report of Food Analyst, is vague. Food Analyst has failed to disclose the name of test which was carried out by him, while detecting the colour in the sample commodity.
